question: One of the basic differences between conventional x-ray and CT scan is that in CT scan
options: stationary x-ray source is used where as in conventional x-ray a rotating x-ray source is used.
a rotating ultrasound source is used whereas in conventional x-ray a stationary x-ray source is used.
many successive images are gained whereas in conventional x-ray a single shadow image is gained.
the image provides inadequate information, whereas in conventional x-ray, the image provides more detailed information.
explanation: CT scans take multiple successive cross-sectional X-ray images from different angles to construct 3D cross-sectional views, whereas a conventional X-ray produces a single 2D shadow image.
